items.title: Accounts created by invitation
items.statement: Admins create accounts for members; members set their own password through a personal one-time link.

items.title: Stay logged in, with control over devices
items.statement: Members stay logged in on their devices for weeks and can see and end their sessions on other devices.

items.title: Roles
items.statement: The system distinguishes members (read and annotate), librarians (maintain the library and access) and admins (additionally manage users and groups).

items.title: Management where the music is
items.statement: Librarians and admins maintain the library, the programmes and the instrument list directly in the views every user works with, and members see the same views without the management options.

items.title: Access by instrument through groups
items.statement: Members of a group get access to all parts tagged with an instrument granted to the group, e.g. group 'Trumpets' reads every trumpet part.

items.title: Access to whole scores
items.statement: A group can be granted all parts of a score, e.g. for the conductor or section leaders.

items.title: Finer and time-limited grants
items.statement: Librarians can grant access per voice (e.g. only 1st trumpet), per concert programme, and until a date.

items.title: Drawing tools
items.statement: Members can mark up their parts with pen, highlighter, eraser, musical stamps and text, and undo mistakes.

items.title: Named annotation sets
items.statement: Members can keep several named sets of markings per part (e.g. one per concert), switch between them, and hide all markings.

depends_on.note: A set can be linked to a programme and is then chosen automatically.

items.title: Markings are never lost
items.statement: Markings are saved automatically and survive closing the tab, network problems and editing on two devices.

items.title: Private markings
items.statement: A member's markings are visible to nobody else, administrators included.

conflicts_with.note: Sharing is explicit and read-only; private sets stay private.

items.title: Markings follow corrected sheets
items.statement: When a librarian replaces a sheet with a corrected version, members keep their markings and can move them to the new version.

items.title: Shared markings for a section
items.statement: A section leader can share a read-only set of markings (e.g. bowings, cuts) with a group.

conflicts_with.note: Sharing is explicit and read-only; private sets stay private.

items.title: Upload sheets as PDF, with versions
items.statement: Librarians can upload a PDF file for each part and later replace it with a corrected version, without losing the previous version.

items.title: Fast and safe delivery of sheets
items.statement: The system delivers sheet files quickly to the musicians allowed to read them, and to nobody else.

items.title: MusicXML sheets
items.statement: Librarians can upload MusicXML files in addition to PDF; members can read them.

items.title: Scores and parts with metadata
items.statement: Librarians can describe each work (score) and each of its sheets (parts) with metadata, and members see the library organised by work.

items.title: Library search
items.statement: Users can find works in the library by title, composer, arranger, genre and tags.

items.title: Extended metadata
items.statement: Librarians can record further information per work: difficulty grade, duration, lyricist, clef of a part, publisher and catalogue number, ensemble type, rights status with expiry, performing-rights information and a reference recording. (The archive number is part of F-LIB-001: R-LIB-015.)

items.title: Encrypted offline app
items.statement: A native app stores the member's sheets and markings encrypted on the device, works without network, and synchronises when online.

conflicts_with.note: F-SEC-001 applies to the web client. The app stores data only encrypted, with a key in the OS keystore and a time-limited offline lease.

items.title: Simple installation
items.statement: The system is installed as one program or one container, with all data in one directory.

items.title: Backup and restore
items.statement: Operators can make a consistent backup while the system runs and restore it.

items.title: Health monitoring
items.statement: Operators and container platforms can check automatically whether the system works.

items.title: Encrypted connections
items.statement: All traffic between devices and server can be encrypted (HTTPS), with little effort for the operator.

items.title: Runs on small hardware
items.statement: The server runs on a Raspberry Pi 4 or a virtual server with 1 vCPU and 1 GB RAM.

items.title: Everyone opens the same piece at once
items.statement: The system serves a whole ensemble that opens the same piece within the same few seconds without noticeable delay.

items.title: Concert programmes
items.statement: Librarians can put together concert programmes: a dated, ordered list of works, which members open as a set list.

required_by.note: A set can be linked to a programme and is then chosen automatically.

items.title: Prepare a programme in advance
items.statement: When a member opens a programme, all their sheets of it are downloaded ahead of time, so that playing needs no network.

conflicts_with.note: Prefetched sheets are held in memory only, never stored on the device; a reload downloads them again.

items.title: Stage-ready reader
items.statement: Members read their parts one page at a time, fitted to the screen, turn pages without looking away from the music, and the screen stays on.

items.title: Move through a programme while reading
items.statement: While reading a part from a programme, the member reaches the previous and next piece directly from the reader.

items.title: System view for small screens
items.statement: Besides whole pages, members can read their parts as a sequence of whole music systems: as many systems as fit at a chosen minimum staff size, cropped to the width of the music and continuing across page boundaries, so the notes stay readable on a small tablet. The server finds the systems of every uploaded file automatically; pages it is unsure about are shown whole, and librarians can correct the detection.

items.title: Nothing stored on the device
items.statement: The web client stores no sheets, markings or other data persistently on the device.

conflicts_with.note: F-SEC-001 applies to the web client. The app stores data only encrypted, with a key in the OS keystore and a time-limited offline lease.
Prefetched sheets are held in memory only, never stored on the device; a reload downloads them again.

items.title: Protection against common attacks
items.statement: The system resists password guessing, cross-site request forgery, injection and probing of the library, and stores secrets only in non-reversible form.

items.title: Rust backend and Dioxus client
items.statement: The server is written in Rust; the user interface is written in Rust with Dioxus.

items.title: Central sheet music library
items.statement: The ensemble keeps its sheet music in one digital library that librarians maintain and members use.

items.title: The right parts reach the right musicians
items.statement: Every musician gets exactly the parts they play, without the librarian having to assign each file to each person.

items.title: Personal markings
items.statement: Every musician can add their own markings to their parts, keep them, and use different markings for different concerts, without changing the original sheet.

items.title: Reliable paperless playing
items.statement: Musicians can read and turn their parts on a tablet during rehearsals and concerts as reliably as on paper, even when the whole ensemble opens the same piece at the same moment.

items.title: Simple and cheap to run
items.statement: A volunteer-run ensemble can install, operate and back up the system on small, inexpensive hardware without special knowledge.

items.title: Protect members and the library
items.statement: Accounts, personal markings and the (often licensed) sheet music are protected against unauthorised access and loss.

items.title: Offline use and more formats in the future
items.statement: The system can later be extended by an app that works offline with encrypted local storage, and by sheet formats other than PDF.

items.title: Maintainable technology
items.statement: The system is built with a small, consistent technology stack that a small team can maintain over years.

items.title: Create accounts with an invite link
items.statement: When an admin creates a user (username, display name, role), the system shall create the account without password and return a one-time invite link valid for 7 days.

items.title: Accept an invite
items.statement: When a user opens a valid invite link and chooses a password of 8 to 256 characters, the system shall set the password, invalidate all invites and sessions of that user, and log the user in.

items.title: First administrator
items.statement: When the server starts with no users, it shall create the user 'admin' without password and write a one-time invite link for it to the log.

items.title: Login
items.statement: The system shall log a user in with username (any letter case) and password, and shall answer wrong usernames and wrong passwords identically, also in response time.

items.title: Long-lived sessions
items.statement: The system shall keep a session valid for a configurable number of days since its last use (default 60).

items.title: See and end sessions
items.statement: The system shall show users their active sessions (device, last use) and let them end any of them; logging out ends the current one.

items.title: Change password
items.statement: When a user changes their password, the system shall require the current password and end all other sessions of that user.

items.title: Disable users
items.statement: When an admin disables a user, the system shall end all sessions and invites of that user and refuse further logins, while keeping the user's annotations; admins shall not be able to disable themselves or remove their own admin role.

items.title: Rights of the roles
items.statement: The system shall allow members to read granted parts and annotate them; librarians additionally to manage scores, parts, files, programmes, instruments and grants; admins additionally to manage users, groups and group membership.

items.title: Password reset by new invite
items.statement: When an admin requests a new invite for an enabled user, the system shall replace any previous invite of that user with a new one-time link.

items.title: Login through an identity provider
items.statement: The system shall allow users to log in through an external OpenID Connect provider (e.g. Keycloak, Authentik, Google) configured by the operator.

items.title: Send invite links by e-mail
items.statement: When an operator configured an SMTP server, the system shall offer to send invite and reset links to the user's e-mail address.

items.title: Management actions inside the regular views
items.statement: When a librarian or admin is logged in, the web client shall offer the management actions in the regular views: adding a piece and editing each piece and each part in the library, creating and editing programmes in the programme views, and adding, editing and deleting instruments in the instrument list; groups (librarians and admins) and users (admins) shall have their own navigation entries, and there shall be no separate management area.

items.title: Members see the same views without management options
items.statement: When a member is logged in, the web client shall show the library, programme and instrument views without any control to add, edit or delete, and the server shall keep refusing every management request of a member regardless of the user interface.

items.title: Assignments scale to many entries
items.statement: When a librarian or admin assigns users, instruments or scores to a group, instruments to a part, or pieces to a programme, the web client shall show only the assigned entries as a list, each with a remove control, and offer the other entries in a dropdown with a search field instead of one checkbox per existing entry.

items.title: Several entries chosen at once, applied when the dropdown closes
items.statement: When the assignment dropdown is open, ticking an entry shall not close it, and closing it by clicking or tapping outside, by pressing Escape, or with its "Add" button shall add all ticked entries to the assigned list.

items.title: Assignments of existing groups and parts are saved immediately
items.statement: When the assignments of an existing group or an existing part change, by closing the dropdown with new entries or by removing an entry, the web client shall save the change at once, confirm it briefly with "Saved", and on failure show the error and restore the previous list.

items.title: Read rule
items.statement: The system shall let a user read a part if the user is a librarian or admin, or a member of a group that is granted one of the part's instruments, or a member of a group that is granted the part's score.

items.title: Denied as not found
items.statement: The system shall answer requests for parts, files, programmes and annotations the user may not read exactly like requests for things that do not exist (HTTP 404).

items.title: Changes apply immediately
items.statement: The system shall apply changes to groups, memberships and grants to the next request of every affected user, without new login.

items.title: Managing groups and grants
items.statement: The system shall let admins create, rename and delete groups and set their members, and let librarians set the instruments and scores granted to a group.

items.title: Grants per voice
items.statement: The system shall allow granting an instrument to a group for selected voices only (e.g. Trumpet voice 1), using the voices stored with each part (R-LIB-002): a part is readable through such a grant when it contains at least one of the granted voices.

items.title: Grants per programme and until a date
items.statement: The system shall allow granting a group all pieces of a programme, and shall allow any grant to expire at a given date.

items.title: Several ensembles on one server
items.statement: The system shall allow one server to host several independent ensembles, each with its own users, groups, instruments, library and programmes that the other ensembles cannot see.

items.title: Pen and highlighter
items.statement: The web client shall let members draw freehand with a pen (4 colours, 3 widths, width following pen pressure) and a semi-transparent highlighter (3 colours) that is drawn below pen strokes.

items.title: Eraser, stamps and text
items.statement: The web client shall let members erase whole objects by touching them, place musical stamps (breath mark, fermata, glasses, sharp, flat, natural, accent, caesura) with one tap, and place short text notes.

items.title: Undo and redo
items.statement: The web client shall let members undo and redo their changes on the current page.

items.title: Palm rejection
items.statement: Once a pen was used in the reader, the web client shall ignore touch input for drawing.

items.title: Device-independent position
items.statement: The system shall store annotation positions relative to the page, so that markings appear at the same place in the music on every screen size and zoom level.

items.title: Limits of an annotation page
items.statement: The system shall reject annotation pages with more than 20 000 objects, strokes with more than 20 000 points, texts longer than 1 000 characters, encodings larger than 4 MiB, duplicate object ids, or malformed content (HTTP 422).

items.title: Compact storage
items.statement: The system shall store a typical annotated page (30 strokes of 60 points) in less than 12 KB before compression.

items.title: Annotation sets
items.statement: The system shall let members create, rename, duplicate (with all pages), and delete named annotation sets per part, with names unique per member and part, mark exactly one set per part as default, and link a set to a programme.

items.title: Choosing the set when reading
items.statement: When the reader opens, the web client shall show the set linked to the current programme, else the default set; when a member draws without any set, it shall create one named after the programme or 'My annotations'; members can switch sets or hide all markings.

items.title: Automatic saving
items.statement: The web client shall save a changed page 1.5 s after the last change, immediately when turning the page or leaving the reader, and show whether all changes are saved.

items.title: Saving when the tab closes
items.statement: When the tab is closed or reloaded while changes are unsaved, the web client shall still send them to the server.

items.title: Editing on two devices
items.statement: The system shall detect when a page was saved by another device in the meantime (revision check), and the web client shall then merge both versions so that additions and deletions from both devices are kept.

items.title: Pages without markings
items.statement: The system shall answer requests for an annotation page that was never saved as an empty page with revision 0, not as an error.

items.title: Only the owner sees annotations
items.statement: The system shall let only the member who created an annotation set read, change or delete it; no other user, administrators included, can access it through the system.

items.title: Annotations follow access
items.statement: When a member loses access to a part, the system shall hide the member's annotations on it without deleting them, and show them again if access is granted again.

items.title: Sets belong to a file version
items.statement: The system shall bind every annotation set to the file version it was drawn on, show the member when a newer version exists, and move the set to the current version on request if the page count is unchanged; otherwise it shall refuse the move.

items.title: Share a set read-only
items.statement: The system shall let a member share one of their sets read-only with a group whose members may read the same part.

items.title: Encrypted annotations at rest
items.statement: The system shall store annotation layers encrypted with a key per user, so that access to the database file alone does not reveal them.

items.title: Simple shapes
items.statement: The web client shall let members draw straight lines, rectangles and ellipses as annotation objects.

items.title: Readable export of annotations
items.statement: The system shall let members (and developers for debugging) export an annotation set as JSON.

items.title: Accepted uploads
items.statement: The system shall accept as part file only PDF files (recognised by their content) up to a configurable size, by default 200 MB.

items.title: File versions
items.statement: When a librarian uploads a file with different content for a part, the system shall add it as a new version and keep all previous versions readable; uploading the current content again shall not create a version.

items.title: Page count and thumbnail
items.statement: When a PDF is uploaded, the system shall determine its page count and create a thumbnail of the first page; if the PDF cannot be analysed, it shall store the file anyway without this information.

items.title: Immutable, content-addressed storage
items.statement: The system shall store every file once under its SHA-256 hash, never modify or overwrite a stored file, and write it so that a stored file is always complete.

conflicts_with.note: Files stay immutable; only unreferenced files are removed, and only after a grace period so that older backups stay consistent.
The personalised copy is generated on delivery and never stored as a blob; the original stays immutable and content-addressed.

items.title: Access check on every download
items.statement: The system shall deliver a file or thumbnail only to users who may read at least one part using that file, and answer all other requests as if the file did not exist (HTTP 404).

items.title: Conditional and partial downloads
items.statement: The system shall mark every file with its hash as ETag, answer a matching If-None-Match with HTTP 304, and answer Range requests with the requested bytes (HTTP 206).

items.title: Configurable client caching
items.statement: The system shall by default forbid clients to store downloaded files (Cache-Control: private, no-store), and shall allow operators to permit private caching of files instead.

conflicts_with.note: No-store means every reload downloads the sheets again; operators who accept browser caches can switch to 'immutable'.

items.title: MusicXML upload
items.statement: The system shall accept MusicXML files (.musicxml and compressed .mxl) as part files and extract title, composer and part names from them.

items.title: Removal of unused files
items.statement: The system shall offer operators a way to delete stored files that no part version and no annotation set references any more, after a grace period.

conflicts_with.note: Files stay immutable; only unreferenced files are removed, and only after a grace period so that older backups stay consistent.

items.title: Smaller scanned sheets
items.statement: When a scanned PDF is uploaded, the system shall offer to store an optimised version with bilevel image compression (CCITT G4 or JBIG2) if it is substantially smaller.

items.title: Score metadata
items.statement: The system shall store for each score a title (required, at most 200 characters) and optionally a subtitle, composer, arranger, genre, a list of up to 30 tags, notes, and an archive number (R-LIB-015).

items.title: Part metadata
items.statement: The system shall store for each part an optional custom name, one or more instruments, an ordered list of up to 10 voices (none, one or several; each free text of up to 20 characters, e.g. '2', '1a', 'Solo'), an optional key (R-LIB-011), and notes. It shall store the voices so that it knows which voices a part contains (R-ACL-005), keep their order, ignore blank entries and drop repeated voices, ignoring letter case.

items.title: Controlled instrument vocabulary
items.statement: The system shall keep instruments as a list maintained by librarians, with unique names (ignoring letter case), and shall refuse to delete an instrument that parts still use.

items.title: Search
items.statement: The system shall find scores for which every entered word is a word prefix of the title, subtitle, composer, arranger, genre, tags or archive number (R-LIB-015), or of the name of a part of the score the user may read (R-LIB-010), ignoring letter case and diacritics, and shall additionally filter by genre and tag.

items.title: Members see only their part of the library
items.statement: The system shall list for a member only scores with at least one part the member may read, and within them only those parts; librarians and admins see all scores and parts.

items.title: Thumbnails in the library
items.statement: The web client shall show for each readable part a thumbnail of its first page, if the server could create one.

items.title: Extended score metadata
items.statement: The system shall store for each score optionally a lyricist, a difficulty grade (1–6), a duration (minutes and seconds), publisher and catalogue number, ensemble type, rights status (owned, rented until a date, public domain), a performing-rights work number and a link to a reference recording, and for each part optionally its clef (e.g. treble or bass; trombone and euphonium parts exist in both).

items.title: Instrument list for every user
items.statement: The system shall show every logged-in user the instruments of the ensemble with their family, grouped by family.

items.title: Guided flow for adding a piece
items.statement: When a librarian adds a piece, the web client shall guide them in two visible steps, first the score details and then its parts, where each part is entered with label, instruments, voices, key and an optional PDF, several parts can be added one after another, and the upload state of every added part is shown.

items.title: Part names derived from instruments, key and voices
items.statement: When a part has no custom name, the system shall name it after its instruments, key and voices in the form "<instruments joined by ' / ' in alphabetical order> in <key> <voices joined by ' & ' in their order>", and shall show this name, or the custom name if one is given, wherever the part is shown.

items.title: Keys from a fixed list
items.statement: The system shall accept as key of a part only none (concert pitch) or one of B♭, E♭, F, C, A, D, G, E, A♭, D♭, G♭ and B♮ (H), stored as the codes Bb, Eb, F, C, A, D, G, E, Ab, Db, Gb and H, and the web client shall offer exactly these in a selection list.

items.title: Existing parts survive the change of part names
items.statement: When a database created before part names were derived is opened, the system shall keep every existing label as the custom name, keep numeric voices as text, convert key spellings that are unambiguous to the key codes, keep all other key values unchanged, and make the parts findable by name.

items.title: Tags entered as chips
items.statement: When a librarian edits the tags of a piece, the web client shall show every finished tag as a non-editable chip like the tags in the library, with a remove button, and a text field before, between or after the chips for the next tag.

items.title: Suggestions of existing tags and families
items.statement: While a librarian types a tag of a piece or the family of an instrument, the web client shall show a small list of the existing tags or families that match the typed text, ignoring letter case and diacritics, those starting with the text first, without the tags the piece already has.

items.title: Archive number of a piece
items.statement: The system shall store for each score optionally an archive number: free text of at most 40 characters (e.g. "0304" or "A-12"), trimmed, an empty entry meaning none. The number is not required to be unique. The library shall show it with the piece, shall find a piece by it (also without leading zeros or separators: "304" finds "0304", "A12" finds "A-12") and shall offer to sort the list by it in natural order ("28" before "304").

items.title: Encrypted local storage
items.statement: The app shall store sheets and annotations only encrypted, with a random key per device protected by the operating system's keystore.

items.title: Synchronisation
items.statement: The app shall synchronise sheets by file hash and annotations by page revision, transferring only what changed.

items.title: Offline lease and revocation
items.statement: The app shall delete local data it is no longer allowed to read at the next synchronisation, and discard its key when it has not synchronised for a configurable time (default 30 days).

items.title: One program, one data directory
items.statement: The system shall run as a single server program that serves the API and the web client and keeps all data (database and files) in one configurable directory.

items.title: Configuration
items.statement: The server shall read every setting from a command-line option or an equivalent MUSICUS_* environment variable.

items.title: Container
items.statement: The project shall provide a container image and a Compose file that start the system with persistent data in a volume.

items.title: Automatic migrations
items.statement: When the server starts, it shall bring the database schema to the current version automatically.

items.title: Online backup
items.statement: The system shall provide a command that writes a consistent copy of the database while the server runs.

items.title: HTTPS
items.statement: The system shall support HTTPS either directly (certificate and key files) or behind a reverse proxy, and the project shall provide a Compose profile with automatic certificates.

items.title: Health check
items.statement: The system shall answer GET /api/health without login with 'ok' when it can read its database, and provide a 'healthcheck' command that exits with 0 only in that case.

items.title: Graceful shutdown
items.statement: When the server receives SIGTERM or Ctrl-C, it shall stop accepting connections and let running requests finish.

items.title: Continuous database replication
items.statement: The system shall support continuous replication of the database to another location (e.g. with Litestream), so that it can be restored to a recent point in time.

items.title: Memory use
items.statement: The server shall use less than 50 MB of memory when idle and run on a Raspberry Pi 4 (arm64) and on a virtual server with 1 vCPU and 1 GB RAM.

items.title: Bounded password hashing
items.statement: The server shall run at most as many password hash computations at the same time as it has CPU cores.

items.title: Burst of downloads
items.statement: The server shall serve 120 simultaneous downloads of the same 3 MB file in less than 1 s of server time on one CPU core.

items.title: Hot files in memory
items.statement: The server shall keep recently delivered files in a memory cache of configurable size (default 128 MB), evicting the least recently used, and share one copy between all simultaneous downloads.

items.title: Fast access check
items.statement: The server shall decide whether a user may read a part in less than 1 ms for a library of 200 000 parts.

items.title: Concurrent annotation saves
items.statement: The server shall store 120 simultaneous annotation page saves in less than 1 s on one CPU core.

items.title: Playing without network
items.statement: Once a programme was prepared, the web client shall be able to show and turn all its pages without further sheet downloads.

conflicts_with.note: No-store means every reload downloads the sheets again; operators who accept browser caches can switch to 'immutable'.

items.title: System detection budget
items.statement: The server shall detect the systems of an A4 page in at most 250 ms on one core of an x86-64 laptop (about one second on a Raspberry Pi 4), with one background worker, rendering at most 1754 × 1754 pixels per page, so that analysing a new file never delays requests.

items.title: Programme content
items.statement: The system shall store for each programme a title, an optional date (YYYY-MM-DD), notes, and an ordered list of up to 200 scores in which a score may appear more than once.

items.title: Members see their programmes
items.statement: The system shall show a member only programmes that contain at least one piece the member has a readable part for, and within them only those pieces with only those parts.

items.title: Prefetch the sheets of an opened programme
items.statement: When a member opens a programme, the web client shall start downloading every readable sheet of it into memory, at most 3 at a time, and show the progress and any failed downloads.

conflicts_with.note: Sheets are kept in memory only; a reload downloads them again.

items.title: Free memory of other programmes
items.statement: When a member opens a programme, the web client shall release the in-memory sheets of all other programmes.

items.title: Page display
items.statement: The web client shall show one page at a time, scaled to fit the available space, rendered at the device's pixel density, and without blank flashes when the page changes.

items.title: Turning pages
items.statement: In reading mode, the web client shall turn to the next page on a tap in the right third or on Arrow Right, Arrow Down, Page Down or Space, and to the previous page on a tap in the left third or on Arrow Left, Arrow Up or Page Up.

items.title: Screen stays on
items.statement: While the reader is open, the web client shall keep the screen from dimming where the browser supports the screen wake lock, and re-acquire it after the tab becomes visible again.

items.title: Full screen
items.statement: The web client shall offer a button that switches the reader to full screen and back.

items.title: Next and previous piece
items.statement: When a part was opened from a programme, the web client shall open the next piece when turning past the last page, open the previous piece when turning back before the first page, prefer a part that shares an instrument with the current one, and download the next piece in advance.

items.title: Compatible PDF rendering
items.statement: The web client shall render PDF pages with a build of pdf.js that also works in older tablet browsers.

items.title: Half-page turns
items.statement: The web client shall offer a mode in which a page turn first replaces only the upper half of the screen with the upper half of the next page.

items.title: Conductor push
items.statement: When the conductor selects the next piece of a programme, the web client of every member reading that programme shall offer to open it.

items.title: Swipe to turn pages
items.statement: In reading mode, the web client shall turn to the next page on a swipe to the left and to the previous page on a swipe to the right.

items.title: Detect music systems of every file
items.statement: The server shall find, for every page of every PDF file, the staves, the music systems they form, the cut lines between the systems, a header above and a footer below them and a confidence value, once per file in the background after the upload, and serve the result to everyone who may read the file at `GET /api/files/{sha256}/layout`.

items.title: Views of whole systems at a minimum staff size
items.statement: In the system view, the web client shall show as many whole systems as fit on the screen at the user's minimum staff height, as one contiguous crop of the original page per page (from the first shown system to the last, including the space and everything between them), cropped to the horizontal extent of the music of the whole part, at one scale for the whole part; a system shall never be cut. If the music is wider than the screen at the minimum height, it shall be shown at the full screen width.

items.title: Turning in the system view
items.statement: In the system view, the keys, pedals, taps and swipes that turn pages shall turn views; if the current view shows at least three systems the next view shall start with its last system (one system overlap), otherwise with the system after it.

items.title: Systems continue across pages
items.statement: The system view shall treat the systems of all pages of a part as one sequence, so that a view may show the last systems of one page and the first systems of the next; after the last view of a part in a programme it shall open the next piece as the page view does.

items.title: View setting per user
items.statement: The reader shall offer a switch between page view and system view and, in the system view, the staff sizes S, M, L and XL (minimum staff height 5, 6, 7 and 8 mm on the screen); the choice shall be stored per user on the server, not on the device.

items.title: Unsure pages are shown whole
items.statement: A page without systems or with a detection confidence below 0.6 shall appear in the system view as one whole page, fitted to the screen, at its place in the sequence; while a file's layout is pending or failed, the reader shall show whole pages and say why.

items.title: Librarians correct the systems
items.statement: A librarian shall be able to correct the detected layout of every page of a file version: move, add and delete cut lines (which merges and splits systems), mark a band as system, header or hidden, and mark a page to be shown whole; the correction shall apply to all members, override the automatic detection and survive a new detection run.

items.title: Split wide systems at a barline
items.statement: When a system is so wide that it cannot reach the minimum staff height, the system view should show it in two halves, divided at a barline near its middle, one below the other.

items.title: Annotations in the system view
items.statement: In the system view, annotations shall be shown on every crop and drawn, erased, stamped and typed there exactly as in the page view, stored in the coordinates of the whole page.

items.title: System layouts of a programme ahead
items.statement: When a member opens a programme, the web client shall also load the system layouts of all its sheets into memory, so that the system view works on stage without network.

conflicts_with.note: Layouts are kept in memory only, like the sheets.

items.title: No persistent data in the web client
items.statement: The web client shall keep sheets and annotations only in memory and shall not use local storage, IndexedDB, the Cache API or a service worker.

conflicts_with.note: Sheets are kept in memory only; a reload downloads them again.
Layouts are kept in memory only, like the sheets.

items.title: Secrets stored irreversibly
items.statement: The system shall store passwords only as Argon2id hashes (19 MiB, 2 iterations, parallelism 1) and session and invite tokens (256-bit random) only as SHA-256 hashes.

items.title: Limit password guessing
items.statement: The system shall refuse login attempts with HTTP 429 after 10 failed attempts within 15 minutes for the same username or the same client address.

items.title: Cross-site request forgery
items.statement: The system shall send the session cookie only as HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and (by default) Secure, and shall reject state-changing requests authenticated by cookie that lack the header x-musicus-csrf (HTTP 403).

items.title: Security headers
items.statement: The system shall send with every response the headers X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: same-origin and a Permissions-Policy that disables camera, microphone and geolocation.

items.title: No SQL injection
items.statement: The system shall use only SQL statements fixed at compile time and pass all user input as bound parameters.

items.title: Minimal, unprivileged container
items.statement: The container image shall contain only the server, the web assets and the C runtime, and run as an unprivileged user.

items.title: No internal details in errors
items.statement: The system shall answer internal errors with a generic message and log the details only on the server.

items.title: Personal watermark
items.statement: The system shall be able to add the name of the downloading member to the margin of every delivered sheet.

conflicts_with.note: The personalised copy is generated on delivery and never stored as a blob; the original stays immutable and content-addressed.

items.title: Download audit log
items.statement: The system shall record which user downloaded which file version and when, and let admins view this log.

items.title: Server technology
items.statement: The server shall be written in Rust and use an embedded SQLite database.

items.title: Client technology
items.statement: The web client shall be written in Rust with Dioxus and compiled to WebAssembly; JavaScript is limited to one bridge module for browser features without Rust equivalent.

items.title: Shared API types
items.statement: Server and clients shall exchange data through a REST API whose request and response types are defined in one shared Rust crate.
